bull.b: Record leasing activity and a $2.5 billion backlog provide durable visibility into future rental revenue. Booked-not-billed capacity should support growth across several years, while strong demand from hyperscale, enterprise, and AI customers reinforces Digital Realty’s market position.

High occupancy, record-low churn, and strong re-leasing spreads indicate valuable, embedded customer relationships and pricing power. These portfolio metrics support recurring cash NOI growth and suggest that demand remains strong enough to sustain favorable economics as leases renew.

bull.t: Improving growth outlook and funding access
bull.b: Raised core FFO guidance and expected double-digit growth reflect expanding earnings capacity, while private capital and substantial funding availability support development without relying solely on operating cash flow. This combination strengthens execution capacity across the global data-center pipeline.

bear.b: Leverage remains meaningful even after recent improvement, and continued debt issuance increases fixed financial obligations. Higher indebtedness can reduce flexibility if development costs rise or operating conditions weaken, while refinancing and interest costs remain important constraints on future capital allocation.

The sharp margin variability and weak TTM cash conversion make reported earnings less predictable than the recurring-revenue model would imply. Capital intensity, working-capital effects, or mix changes may continue to separate accounting profit from distributable cash and complicate funding decisions.

Data-center expansion faces structural constraints involving electricity availability, community acceptance, permitting, construction timing, and project costs. These issues can delay capacity delivery, increase investment requirements, and limit where Digital Realty can deploy its sizable development pipeline.
